correctness.summary: Same-direction selected neighbours are forbidden by uniqueness of 2-geodesics in girth-at-least-five factors. Hence every connected selected induced subgraph has maximum degree at most two. Four consecutive vertices of any longer path or cycle force alternating factor directions, and every endpoint geodesic then meets a selected internal vertex; a 4-cycle fails by the two opposite-corner geodesics. Cartesian corners attain size three, are the only maximizers, and are counted by summing d_G(g)d_H(h). Definition-level small-product verification agrees.

limitations: Both factors are assumed connected, nontrivial, and of girth at least five.
Mixed low-girth factors and products of three or more factors are not classified.
Finite verification supports but does not replace the proof.
The connected invariant is extremely recent, so parallel unindexed work remains an originality risk.
Independent audit has not been performed.

originality.scope: to the best of our knowledge
originality.summary: The September 2026 paper introducing connected mutual visibility does not state a Cartesian-product result in the inspected version. Earlier Cartesian-product literature treats ordinary, total, lower, or game variants rather than the connected maximum parameter. Exact and synonymous searches found no equivalent high-girth-factor theorem or maximizer count. The main residual risk is very recent parallel or not-yet-indexed work because the invariant itself was introduced only days ago.

review_statement: Same-model review: passed. Independent audit: not yet performed.

value.summary: The theorem gives an exact, shape-independent product law for a broad graph class, classifies and counts all maximizers, and yields a constant connected mutual-visibility number on grids even though ordinary mutual visibility grows with the smaller grid dimension.
